# NumberBox

Header: `winui/ui/text/NumberBox.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/text/NumberBox.hpp`.

A text box for a number, validated and formatted when committed. It can have spin buttons, arithmetic input, stepping by keyboard and wheel, and a header.

[value()](#value) is the number that counts. The user can type anything, and the text is committed on Enter, on losing focus and before each step. [Text](text.md#uitext) that parses is clamped to [min, max] and formatted again. [Text](text.md#uitext) that doesn't is replaced by the last value's text. An unset value (the default) means no number, and the box is empty and shows the placeholder. The box is one focus stop and owns its inner [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox). In a spec tree it is built by [`ui::NumberBox`](#uinumberbox).

Example: 
```cpp
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
double quantity = 5.0;

auto box = std::make_unique<ui::NumberBoxControl>(/*value=*/5.0, /*min=*/0.0, /*max=*/100.0);
box->set_header("Quantity");
box->set_spin_button_placement(ui::NumberBoxSpinButtonPlacementMode::Inline);
box->set_step(1.0);
box->set_large_step(10.0);
box->set_accepts_expression(true); // "2 * 3" commits 6
box->set_number_formatter(ui::DecimalFormatter{.fraction_digits = 2});
box->on_value_changed([&](std::optional<double> v) { quantity = v.value_or(0.0); });
ui::NumberBoxControl* quantity_box = stack->add(std::move(box));

// Or declaratively:
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> price{9.5};
stack->add(ui::NumberBox{
    .header                = "Price",
    .placeholder_text      = "0.00",
    .value                 = price,
    .min                   = 0.0,
    .spin_button_placement = ui::NumberBoxSpinButtonPlacementMode::Compact,
}.build());
```

## `ui::NumberBox`

A numeric field, with spin buttons when asked for. Builds a [ui::NumberBoxControl](#uinumberboxcontrol).

Typed text is committed on Enter or when focus leaves. It is parsed, or evaluated with [`.accepts_expression`](#uinumberbox-accepts_expression), clamped to `[min, max]` and reported through [`.on_value_changed`](#uinumberbox-on_value_changed). A bound value outside `[min, max]` is clamped too, and a two-way property gets the clamped value written back. The arrow keys, the wheel and the spin buttons step by [`.step`](#uinumberbox-step).

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<std::optional<double>> quantity{1.0};

window.set_content(ui::NumberBox{
    .header                = "Quantity",
    .value                 = quantity,
    .min                   = 0.0,
    .max                   = 99.0,
    .spin_button_placement = ui::NumberBoxSpinButtonPlacementMode::Inline,
    .accepts_expression    = true,
});
```

```cpp
ui::NumberBox{
    .header, .description, .error, .placeholder_text, .value, .min, .max, .step, .large_step,
    .spin_button_placement, .accepts_expression, .number_formatter, .validation_mode,
    .wrap_enabled, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width,
    .max_height, .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled,
    .accessibility, .on_value_changed, .on_text_changed, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

## `ui::NumberBoxControl`

Derives from `ui::Element`, `ui::RangeValueProvider`.

A text box for a number, validated and formatted when committed. It can have spin buttons, arithmetic input, stepping by keyboard and wheel, and a header.

[value()](#value) is the number that counts. The user can type anything, and the text is committed on Enter, on losing focus and before each step. [Text](text.md#uitext) that parses is clamped to [min, max] and formatted again. [Text](text.md#uitext) that doesn't is replaced by the last value's text. An unset value (the default) means no number, and the box is empty and shows the placeholder. The box is one focus stop and owns its inner [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox). In a spec tree it is built by [`ui::NumberBox`](#uinumberbox).

### set_range

```cpp

```

Sets the range and clamps the current value into it, as [SliderControl::set_range()](slider.md#set_range) does. Fires [on_value_changed()](#on_value_changed) when that changes the value. A [`max`](#max) below [`min`](#min) becomes [`min`](#min).


The committed number, unset for none. Not what is being typed until it commits.

### set_value

```cpp
void set_value(std::optional<double> value)
```

Sets the value, clamped to [min, max] under InvalidInputOverwritten, and formats the text to match. Fires [on_value_changed()](#on_value_changed) only when the value changed. Unset or NaN means no number, and the box is empty.

## Enumerations

### NumberBoxSpinButtonPlacementMode

```cpp
enum class NumberBoxSpinButtonPlacementMode
```

Where a [ui::NumberBox](#uinumberbox) shows its spin buttons.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `Hidden` | No spin buttons (the default); the keyboard and the wheel still step. |
| `Compact` | A small indicator in the box; while it has focus, an up/down button pair floats beside it. Themes without the floating pair show the [Inline](../tree/inline.md) buttons instead. |
| `Inline` | Up and down buttons side by side at the box's right edge; the box is at least 120 DIPs wide. |

### NumberBoxValidationMode

```cpp
enum class NumberBoxValidationMode
```

What a [ui::NumberBox](#uinumberbox) does with input that is not a number.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `InvalidInputOverwritten` | The default: text that does not parse is replaced by the value's text, and committed values are clamped to [min, max]. |
| `Disabled` | No validation: out-of-range values stand and unparsable text is left as typed. |
